verdict.reasoning: Patient describes left arm numbness and tingling for at least two weeks, worsening, involving 2nd–4th fingers and the palmar side: "maybe it's probably been, I'd say for at least two weeks and it's kind of gotten worse"; "second, third and fourth finger"; "it's the...front side".

She notes mild weakness with piano but no dropping objects: "I play a little bit of a piano and so I just noticed that it's...harder to get the notes"; "So you would say there's a mild weakness? Mild, yes"; "have you been dropping things..." "So not so much with the glass".

She reports some pain, though not the main issue: "sometimes I will feel it in my shoulder...feel a little bit of...pain" and earlier jaw pain and right hand knuckle pain. She clarifies the grip issue is from numbness, not pain, but arm/shoulder pain does occur.
She explicitly denies neck pain: Doctor: "Any neck pain at all?" Patient: "No, not. No neck pain."
Doctor confirms no leg involvement: "your weakness is only in your left arm, leg, walking and all this. Normal?" Patient: "Walking is normal. Yeah."

She has taken boxing for a few weeks and injured right knuckles: "I've been taking boxing class for a few weeks"; "I've been taking this boxing class so you know, I kind of heard like my knuckles on my right hand, so that's been a little bit painful."

Massage and warm baths were tried for numbness without benefit, but ibuprofen was for sore muscles/right hand pain, not numbness: "I tried massage, I tried some hot baths and that didn't help with this numbness"; ibuprofen: "my muscles were sore...knuckles on my right hand...I've just kind of taken ibuprofen for that."

She describes transient left peripheral vision loss lasting ~20 minutes that resolved: "I all of a sudden just couldn't see from...my left eye. Like, I lost some, like a little bit of a field of vision"; later: "How long did that episode last for?" "maybe like 20 minutes or so" and it was gone after sleep.

She links the vision loss to the same time period as a prior illness but timing is vague, not clearly "a few weeks after": she had a bad cold a month ago and later says "another weird thing...a few weeks ago is...couldn't see from my left eye". The exact sequence "a few weeks AFTER an illness" is not explicitly stated.

She reports significant fatigue: "sometimes I'll get kind of tired..."; "I just kind of feel this fatigue"; "like this morning, for example, I just felt really fatigued and I couldn't even get myself to the gym."
She reports no ongoing chronic medical problems: "in general, I'm pretty healthy...I work out a lot, and I don't really have any medical problems."
She uses ibuprofen intermittently: "I do take ibuprofen just because my, my muscles were sore a little bit...I've just kind of taken ibuprofen for that."
She reports vitamin D use: "every once in a while I take vitamin D" and later, "But vitamin D, I take."
She takes iron with poor adherence: "my GP really wants me to take iron supplements, but you know, there are this like huge pill, so I, most of the time I just forget."
She reports melatonin use: "and then sometimes I take melatonin to help me sleep."

Doctor states no treatment (e.g., steroids) will be started now: "Should I be taking any drugs or"; Doctor: "No, that's something we can't do...first we need to [adopt] firm diagnosis." No new medications are initiated.
She reports her father has hypothyroidism and autoimmune issues: "my dad has. I don't know if it's hypo. I think it's hypothyroidism...he's got some autoimmune stuff going on."
She lists her mother's conditions: "my mom...she's got diabetes, type 2, she's got hypertension, she's got...high cholesterol."
She denies family neurologic disease: Doctor: "Any neurological conditions in the family?" Patient: "No."

She describes one binge episode but does not comment on usual alcohol habits: "I was out, you know, drinking with friends...we kind of went crazy...I just got uncharacteristically drunk for me." She never explicitly denies regular alcohol use.
She indicates regular exercise: "I work out a lot" and mentions boxing classes and going to the gym.

Assessment elements match HPI: left upper limb numbness, tingling, mild weakness, progressive over ~2 weeks, and worse with activity (boxing): described as "numb...tingling...it's kind of gotten worse"; weakness confirmed; symptoms sometimes with shoulder movement during boxing.

The transient left peripheral vision loss, now resolved, is explicitly discussed: "you mentioned for a while you couldn't see...peripheral vision from your left eye" which lasted ~20 minutes and resolved after sleep.

A recent illness (bad cold/flu-like) is described as past and resolved: "I also had a really bad cold like a month ago...I was sick for probably good, like, two weeks. I was at home...I think I must have had some kind of like a flu or something"; she is not currently describing active symptoms.
Doctor mentions possible multiple sclerosis but does not mention peripheral neuropathy: "Sometimes, you know, you do get things like ms, multiple sclerosis." No peripheral neuropathy is discussed.
Cervical nerve impingement is never discussed in the transcript; only MS and a non-boxing explanation are raised, with consideration of brain scan, but no explicit cervical impingement differential.
Doctor plans an urgent neurology referral: "I'm going to do an urgent, very urgent neurology referral."
Doctor notes specialist may do a brain scan: "What they...might entail is the brain scan and things like that." This is advising MRI/brain imaging pending neurology evaluation.

He advises emergency care for worsening neurologic signs: "if the weakness progresses to your legs or there's any kind of headaches, vomiting, fits, and your visual symptoms are getting worse and not getting better, then that would be an A" (i.e., emergency).
No new medications are started and focus is on monitoring and referral: "Should I be taking any drugs or"; Doctor: "No...first we need to [adopt] firm diagnosis" with no prescriptions given.
